title: How WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail helped CBI crack NEET paper leak
content: A WhatsApp conversation triggered the CBI's probe into the NEET-UG examination scam. Subject matter experts colluded by memorizing exam questions and distributing them to students for a fee. Tracking through Mygate app logs and WhatsApp groups led investigators to the involved students and question setters. Additionally, papers were smuggled to Rajasthan, where coaching centers disseminated the leaked materials. The CBI's chargesheet scrutinizes the organized gang's exploitation of NTA's weaknesses.

title: 'Why should entire city suffer?' Delhi HC on plea for protest at Jantar Mantar
content: Concerns were voiced by the Delhi High Court regarding Jantar Mantar as a protest site, questioning why the city should endure interruptions from protests. A Dalit Christian group has sought permission to hold a peaceful demonstration on August 10, while the police have been tasked to provide clarity on the request by Saturday. Additionally, the Supreme Court is considering other potential protest locations.

title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream
content: Jadumani Singh Mandengbam secured a silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.  He overcame significant selection hurdles and a weight category gamble to achieve this success.  His journey highlights resilience and determination in pursuing his boxing aspirations.  The young boxer's performance was part of India's historic boxing campaign at the Games.

title: Europe's biggest software company SAP pauses travel and hiring over AI costs
content: SAP, Europe's largest tech firm, has halted most travel and hiring. This move supports significant investments in artificial intelligence products and adoption. Only AI-related hiring and essential customer-facing travel are exempt from these new controls. Other companies are also reassessing their AI spending due to rising costs. SAP aims to prioritize spending on future-proofing its enterprise software offerings.

title: Sanchez vs Meloni: Spain imposes Italy border checks as Ceuta migrant row escalates
content: Spain has implemented temporary border checks on travelers arriving by air and sea from Italy, intensifying tensions between these two European Union nations regarding migration policies. Italy had previously enacted similar measures following a significant influx of migrants into Spain. This ongoing conflict underscores the contrasting perspectives on border regulations and the management of migrants within the European Union.

title: Pant's midnight plea to Uttarakhand CM: 'Please help me in land acquisition'
content: Rishabh Pant publicly requested Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami for land. He wishes to shift his base from Delhi to his native state. Pant has been trying to find suitable land for three years without success. He wants to purchase land from the government at applicable rates. Pant recently emerged as Uttarakhand's highest individual taxpayer.

title: 27 Arunachal border locations get standard names to snub China's renaming attempts
content: India has taken a decisive step by officially naming twenty-seven sites in Arunachal Pradesh on its maps, a move designed to clarify territorial boundaries and counter Chinese assertions. These sites represent key historical moments related to border conflicts, featuring important mountains and villages along the McMahon Line, helping to raise awareness of India's rightful claims on these significant lands.

title: Elon Musk's preferred state halts data center approvals, says 'prove' this
content: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has temporarily halted the approval of new data centers while regulators perform a thorough audit of existing projects. Developers are required to demonstrate their electricity and water usage, reflecting a response to mounting concerns surrounding the swift expansion of data centers. The primary focus remains on ensuring the safety and quality of life for all Texans.

title: Widow returns medieval Glastonbury Abbey relic stolen 70 years ago
content: A medieval abbot's kneecap and a floor tile have been returned to Glastonbury Abbey more than 70 years after they were taken by an 11-year-old schoolboy during an archaeological dig. The artefacts were kept in Australia for decades before the boy's widow brought them back following his death in 2025.

title: Houston man’s solo trash cleanups grow into 100-volunteer movement
content: A Houston resident's initiative to clean up neglected areas has blossomed into a vibrant volunteer movement. With one hundred dedicated individuals now on board, their mission is to remove illegally dumped waste. Collaborating with local organizations and harnessing the power of social media, city officials and law enforcement are boosting efforts to tackle this pressing issue, ultimately enhancing the community's aesthetics and the well-being of its residents.

title: Minnesota solar farms turn into wildflower havens, invites bee and butterflies
content: Minnesota solar farms seeded with native plants tripled insect abundance. Native bees increased twentyfold, and more bird species were observed. Taller solar panel arrays allow more native species to grow underneath. Native prairie habitat costs less than gravel over the solar farm's life. Most American solar farms currently lack documented pollinator habitat.

title: Delhi records its wettest August 1st week in 16yrs; yellow alert for today
content: Delhi faced a remarkable deluge yesterday, marking its wettest day of the season and a continuation of rain that has lasted four consecutive days. The city grapples with severe traffic snarls and widespread waterlogging. Reports include the collapse of nine structures and sixteen fallen trees, with Safdarjung weather station noting a staggering 127mm of rain this August. Thankfully, the heavy showers are projected to lessen starting Sunday.

title: Soren govt opens dialogue with Jharkhand student protestors, says talks 'positive'
content: Jharkhand's government held initial discussions with civil service aspirants protesting exam irregularities.  Students stated their demonstrations would persist until concrete government actions were announced.  A ministerial delegation met with representatives of the JSSC-JPSC Reforms Manch.  Protesters demand a CBI probe and cancellation of the 14th JPSC civil services examination.  Support for the ongoing agitation has come from various political and social organizations.

title: Roman Reigns vs. Brock Lesnar net worth in 2026: WWE salaries, earnings & more
content: Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar have contributed to the modern era of WWE. Mostly, with blockbuster rivalries, championship reigns and record-breaking paydays. Reigns is currently the highest-paid on WWE’s active payroll, but Lesnar has made his fortune through WWE, UFC, and premium appearances. An all-out comparison of their projected net worth, career earnings, endorsements, business ventures, investments and future earning potential for 2026.

title: Which tennis queen rules Instagram? Serena, Sabalenka & Osaka lead social race
content: Serena Williams leads active female tennis stars with 17.8 million Instagram followers. Aryna Sabalenka follows with 5.5 million, showcasing her off-court appeal. Naomi Osaka has 3.2 million followers, sharing genuine life updates and mental health discussions. Emma Raducanu and Coco Gauff also maintain significant fanbases with diverse content. Iga Swiatek rounds out the list with her authentic approach to social media.

title: Ronaldo-Georgina wedding: 7 football stars fans won’t expect, including Messi
content: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez are set to tie the knot in an extravagant ceremony this weekend in Madeira. They've secured a historic cathedral and a lavish hotel for the occasion. However, several prominent football figures, like Wayne Rooney and Lionel Messi, may find themselves excluded from the guest list. Other notable absentees are Erik ten Hag and Gary Lineker.

title: India vs Sri Lanka: Captain Shubman Gill's time to take centrestage
content: A year after taking charge of a team in transition, can the captain emerge out of coach Gambhir’s shadow in Sri Lanka?

title: Thailand school shooting: Teen kills grandparents at home, 5 at campus
content: In a tragic event, a teenage student opened fire at a Thai school on Friday, claiming five lives. Prior to the school shooting, he also killed his grandparents. Authorities reported 23 individuals were injured during this violent episode. The weapon used was his grandfather's firearm, unleashing a barrage of shots. This incident represents Thailand's most devastating mass killing in nearly four years.

title: India rejects US criticism of FCRA Bill; MEA calls it 'internal matter'
content: The government is set to expedite the Foreign Contributions Regulation Act, which focuses on managing foreign funding for organizations. In contrast to criticism from a US Congressman regarding proposed changes, the administration remains resolute. Home Minister Amit Shah has met with church leaders to resolve their issues. The Bill's discussion and possible approval in Parliament are imminent.

title: Om Birla seeks proposal for Makar Dwar porch
content: In a recent request, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has called for the construction of a new porch to shield MPs and staff from rain at Makar Dwar. CPWD officials will investigate whether this covered entryway can be constructed, especially as the expenses for the new Parliament House project have surged. The proposed porch will offer a protective haven during vehicle wait times.

title: No government role, don’t endorse Hasina’s remarks at private media event: MEA
content: In a recent statement, India expressed its disapproval of the comments made by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The Ministry of External Affairs emphasized that India was uninvolved in the private media event, leading to Bangladesh's fierce reaction. Dhaka labeled the event as an attack on its sovereignty, asserting that it offends the sentiments of its people and threatens already delicate bilateral relations.

title: 'I got angry': Ashwin reveals why he stopped talking to Sanjay Manjrekar
content: Ravichandran Ashwin opened up about the initial sting from Sanjay Manjrekar's critical comments, which fueled his desire to elevate his fitness and refine his bowling. Manjrekar later praised Ashwin in an article, acknowledging his remarkable performances. As a testament to his skill, Ashwin concluded his career as India's second-highest international wicket-taker with 765 wickets, solidifying his status as one of the country's finest all-rounders, still active in T20 leagues.

title: BJP picks audio clip to target Congress over Karnataka ‘cabinet berths’
content: The BJP has claimed that funds were involved in securing ministerial roles in Karnataka, referencing a leaked audio exchange among Congress officials. BJP representatives have called for clarification from Congress leaders Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, alleging that cabinet positions were obtained through financial means. One BJP leader also raised concerns about the inclusion of an accused figure in the newly formed cabinet.

title: PM Modi's meet with Badal fuels buzz about BJP-SAD pact
content: Sukhbir Singh Badal, the president of the Shiromani Akali Dal, recently met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, igniting discussions about a possible revival of their political alliance in Punjab. While the BJP has declared intentions to run independently in the upcoming elections, support for reconnecting with the Akali Dal exists among some state leaders. This split could inadvertently benefit the Aam Aadmi Party amid multifaceted party dynamics.

title: Ex-HC judge on West Bengal SIR tribunal in Supreme Court seeking protection
content: A former judge of the Calcutta High Court has approached the Supreme Court for protection, citing numerous death threats issued to her and her family ahead of elections. Reports indicate that they received threatening letters, and CCTV wires were tampered with at their residence. Despite submitting complaints, local police failed to provide adequate safety measures.

title: Prime Minister flags Parliament disruptions with new NDA entrants
content: Prime Minister Modi highlighted the unwavering stability of his administration since 2014, remarking on the contrasting volatility of leadership in Britain. He embraced new members into the NDA coalition, asserting that their partnership is attuned to regional interests and developmental needs. Additionally, Modi underscored the critical necessity for growth in eastern India, showcasing a dedication to inclusive progress.

title: Jana Nayagan box office day 16: Thalapathy Vijay film earns Rs 1.18 cr, down 26.2%
content: On its sixteenth day of release, 'Jana Nayagan', featuring Thalapathy Vijay, saw a decline in box office performance, securing Rs 1.18 crore for its India net collection. This brings its global earnings to an impressive Rs 310.03 crore. In a different vein, R. Madhavan's 'G.D.N.' kicked off its run with a humble Rs 59 lakh in gross collections on the first day across Indian theaters.

title: Opposition wants Amit Shah in House; government says 'not your call'
content: Opposition protests continue, lampooning Home Minister Amit Shah for his absence from Parliament.  Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju stated the opposition cannot dictate ministerial attendance.  He asserted Shah is actively working and his presence deters extremists and terrorists.  Opposition MPs disrupted proceedings, demanding Shah address police action against protesters.  The Lok Sabha passed a bill amid the din, with further confrontation anticipated.

title: US sanctions Dubai-based crypto exchange over alleged IRGC funding
content: The United States sanctioned Dubai-based Shelbit for processing millions for Iran's state entities. This action targets sanctions evasion through cryptocurrency networks, as announced by the Treasury Department. Shelbit allegedly facilitated transactions for Iran's central bank and the IRGC. The exchange denied all allegations and stated operations ceased in January 2026. Dubai's regulator also previously found Shelbit violated anti-money laundering rules.

title: Supeme Court to Mahua: Freedom fighters faced bullets, you fear eggs
content: The Supreme Court denied Mahua Moitra's appeal for a virtual appearance in front of the police, as she expressed concerns over potential mob violence and egg-throwing incidents. In response, the court referenced the sacrifices of freedom fighters, suggesting that her fears may be unfounded. The session was overseen by Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, with the MP's legal team advocating for video conferencing.

title: Tribunal reforms bill gets nod, paves way for national body
content: The Cabinet has approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill, which establishes a National Tribunal Commission. This independent body will oversee appointments and functioning of approximately sixteen tribunals. The Supreme Court had previously directed the government to constitute this commission. Concerns were raised about tribunals becoming a liability for the judiciary. The bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha soon.

title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
content: The Supreme Court has requested records from Bihar regarding a minister's appointment. This minister was not an assembly member and faced a six-month deadline. He was later nominated as an MLC, which the government claims resolves the issue. The petitioner cited a 2001 judgment on non-legislator minister re-appointments. The court seeks documents on his initial appointment and subsequent re-induction.

title: I&B ministry eyeing framework to regulate OTT content
content: The I&B ministry is exploring new legislation targeting OTT platforms. This proposed framework prioritizes the regulation of offensive content while preserving users' rights. Plans include implementing robust age verification mechanisms and parental controls. Additionally, an independent review panel will be tasked with evaluating flagged content following its release and determining appropriate sanctions for any breaches of the established guidelines.

title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government
content: The government has staunchly defended the Research, Development and Innovation Fund's comprehensive framework. Officials have emphasized that the presence of strict conflict-of-interest protocols in public funding decisions is paramount. They asserted that a basic professional relationship does not breach any regulations, and measures such as full disclosure and recusal help maintain equitable assessment of all initiatives. For decades, the Technology Development Board has upheld these essential safeguards.

title: Supreme Court dismisses Bofors appeal, 4-decade-old case closed
content: The Supreme Court has officially dismissed an appeal that sought to challenge a 2005 Delhi High Court ruling, effectively concluding the contentious Bofors pay-off case. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal, who filed the appeal, requested an adjournment, but the court declined to extend the timeline on this matter dating back to 2018, which involved accusations against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors.

title: India urges China for river cooperation, presses for data sharing
content: India and China participated in candid discussions regarding border conditions, taking stock of the current landscape along the Line of Actual Control. New Delhi highlighted the necessity of maintaining peace for the advancement of their bilateral relationship. Furthermore, India sought an expedited meeting on the expert committee for trans-border rivers amidst China's unveiling of a significant dam project upstream.

title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
content: Two Indian seafarers remain missing after a drone attack on a merchant ship.  Intense search operations have yielded no sign of the missing sailors.  The government informed the Supreme Court about the grim situation.  The court directed facilitation of maritime insurance payments for the families.  This ensures support for the affected families during this difficult time.

title: Air India announces pay hikes for pilots, raises salary by up to 15%
content: Air India has announced a significant pay rise for pilots, ranging from eight to fifteen percent, with commanders seeing the most substantial hikes. In a strategic move to resolve fleet shortages and improve career advancement opportunities, first officers will gain command upgrades at Air India Express first. Moreover, the airline plans to resume its international flight services next month, marking a return to normal operations.

title: Delhi high court stays food regulator's ban on certain Dabur products
content: The Delhi High Court has temporarily halted an FSSAI directive that questioned Dabur India's product claims. Acknowledging Dabur's established market presence, the court provided initial relief. The order from FSSAI was deemed unjust, as it was issued without company representation. Dabur emphasized that the FSSAI's approach contravened principles of natural justice. The case is set for a further hearing on August 24.

title: NCAER research says Bihar booze ban hasn't worked; lift it, fund development work
content: A recent study advocates for the removal of prohibition in Bihar to foster state growth and enhance capital spending. It posits that banning alcohol hasn't curbed crime rates but instead has spurred illicit activities. By abolishing the prohibition, the state could potentially enjoy a tax revenue boost of 14 to 15 percent.

content: As the Kerala and Madras High Courts examine demands for menstrual leave, only five States have adopted menstrual leave policies, while India has no national law on the issue

Apart from the main theme, that is education, it also brought out issues of urban renewal, cities, middle class, merit and more. To discuss this, we are joined by Krishna Byre Gowda, Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development. Gowda has been in the news for his swift action plans towards making Bengaluru more pedestrian friendly, among other things.
